title: BlueLattice procurement & SLA handoff
next_steps: Maya to send updated MSA redline by 2026-11-27
Liam to produce a short perf spreadsheet (latency/cost) for their sample workload by 2026-11-30
Redwood to share SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation link (security docs) by 2026-11-26
Customer to confirm preferred deployment lane (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) by 2026-12-02
Schedule pilot kickoff for first week of Dec, tentatively 2026-12-03

Liam O'Connor: run 1k-concurrent-req benchmark against dedicated profile and share numbers; due 2026-11-30

summary: Procurement/Legal intake between Redwood AE/SE and BlueLattice procurement + security. Main topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds for latency and uptime, KMS/egress/KPI expectations, pricing path (reserved vs usage), and pilot timeline. Action items agreed; Redwood to send security artifacts and perf snapshot. Customer to choose deployment lane and return top MSA concessions.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we can see a full room here from BlueLattice — quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Liam and Priya are with me; Liam is our SE, Priya handles private deployments and infra. Tom, Sasha, Aria, thanks for being here.

[00:18] Aria Patel: Hi Maya, hi team. We have Procurement, Legal, Sec and Platform on this call — trying to get alignment on the MSA path and the SLA expectations. We've got some internal timelines - finance wants a decision by mid-Dec.

[00:30] Daniel Reyes: From platform perspective we care about consistent p95 latency for short chat flows (< 1s ideally) and, importantly, data residency and keying — we may need KMS that we control.

[00:45] Liam O'Connor: Totally. For the latency target you're describing we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private; Hosted can be tuned but you'd see more variance during spikes. For 1s p95 on multi-turn chat with 2k context, Dedicated is the safer lane.

[01:05] Sasha Kline: On security, SOC 2 docs please, and we need to confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys / HSM. Also retention policy — our legal team is picky about records.

[01:20] Jon Park: We can support customer KMS via our Private deployment and VPC config; there's also an option for a bring-your-own-KMS integration for Dedicated with some additional controls. We'll surface the exact HSM partners.

[01:40] Tom Wu: On the MSA redline we pushed three main asks: stricter data deletion windows, indemnity carveouts for training data, and audit access for our security team. Can you walk through Redwood's standard positions?

[02:02] Maya Chen: Sure. For data deletion we have standard 30 day hot retention by default but offer shorter windows on Private deployments; we can add a contractual clause for faster purging in the DPA. On training/learning: Redwood's hosted models don't automatically ingest customer PII into model training; we can add explicit language. For audits we provide SOC2 report and can support limited audit scope — full on-site audits are uncommon but we can negotiate.

[02:35] Aria Patel: 30 days is probably the maximum we'd accept in Hosted — can you confirm Private would support immediate purge upon request?

[02:45] Priya Nambiar: Yes, Private gives you full control; we can do purge-on-request and we can confirm logs are retained per your retention schedule in the config. There's an additional operational step to verify purge across KV cache and cold storage, but it's doable.

[03:05] Maggie Ortiz: Can we talk pricing structure. We have an existing budget model that prefers fixed committed spend for predictability — curious about reserved capacity discounts and how switching lanes mid-contract affects fees.

[03:19] Liam O'Connor: Reserved (Dedicated) is typically a monthly commit with a significant discount vs on-demand hosted per-token. We can model step-up capacity and burst credits. If you move from Hosted to Dedicated mid-term, billing can be pro-rated and we can credit prior usage toward a committed volume in some cases. We'll put exact numbers in the pricing worksheet.

[03:44] Daniel Reyes: We also need to model egress fees, especially for embedding workloads that pull large datasets for vector search. Any typical egress charge?

[03:54] Maya Chen: Egress is dependent on deployment lane and region — for Private there's no inter-cloud egress from Redwood; for Hosted there can be egress fees tied to data-out to other clouds. We'll include egress assumptions in the sheet.

[04:12] Tom Wu: Back to SLA — uptime numbers? We need commitments for 99.9 vs 99.95. Also a definition for latency SLOs and remedies if thresholds are missed.

[04:26] Priya Nambiar: Our Dedicated SLAs start at 99.9% with options to tier up to 99.95 for higher commits. Latency SLOs are defined per model/route — we'll capture p50/p95/p99 targets for the demo model. Remedies include service credits; full indemnity/termination terms are in the MSA negotiation.

[04:46] Sasha Kline: For incident response we need runbooks, postmortems, and escalation paths. Is there token-level tracing we can hook into?

[04:57] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Console exposes request traces, per-token cost breakdown and we can send traces to your tracing system via a webhook or SIEM integration. For on-call escalation, we'll provide an on-call contact for Dedicated customers.

[05:15] Aria Patel: On data residency — we are regulated in EU and will need EU data residency. Does Redwood have EU regions and can you guarantee data location in contract?

[05:25] Maya Chen: We have EU regions for Hosted and can place Dedicated pools in EU. For Private you can run in your on-prem or VPC in a chosen region — we can add data residency clauses to the DPA.

[05:40] Tom Wu: A couple of legal nuance questions: 1) Limitation of liability caps tied to fees — acceptable? 2) Will Redwood accept carveouts for confirmed breaches?

[05:55] Jon Park: We usually do a liability cap tied to the prior 12 months of fees; for regulated customers there is room to negotiate on a case by case basis. Carveouts for gross negligence are standard; we try to avoid open-ended liability.

[06:12] Maggie Ortiz: Timeline pressure — finance needs final pricing and route choice in ~2.5 weeks. Can Redwood meet that?

[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes — action: I'll send MSA redline by Friday 11/27 and a pricing worksheet within 48 hours of this call. Liam will run the perf bench and Priya will draft the Private deployment checklist.

[06:30] Daniel Reyes: For the pilot acceptance criteria: we want <1.2s p95 for short chat path, 99.9% availability during business hours, and automated logs to be ingested into our Sumo/Datadog. Also a run at 1k concurrent users for 5 minutes without degradation.

[06:52] Liam O'Connor: Noted — we'll validate the 1k concurrent simulation using a dedicated instance profile. We'll record a runbook and include telemetry hooks.

[07:05] Aria Patel: Are there any standard procurement blockers you've seen from similar healthcare buyers?

[07:15] Maya Chen: Common ones: KMS keying questions, indemnity language around PHI, and data locality clauses. For PHI we recommend Private or a high-tier Dedicated plus BAA — Redwood can enter into a BAA for covered use-cases; we'll loop legal to confirm.

[07:32] Tom Wu: BAA is important. Please surface the required controls and any SOC2 controls mapping we'll need to show our auditors.

[07:42] Sasha Kline: Also please clarify where logs live and who has access — we need to ensure min access by Redwood personnel.

[07:51] Jon Park: We'll provide a controls mapping (SOC2/ISO) and a minimal-access policy for the deployment; for Private you get full admin control. For Dedicated we can offer RBAC and SAC approval flows.

[08:05] Maggie Ortiz: A quick question on switching lanes later: if we start Hosted and later move to Dedicated, are there migration costs?

[08:12] Priya Nambiar: There can be migration work depending on model formats and latency tuning; typically a one-time onboarding fee to configure the Dedicated pools and network. We'll estimate that in the pricing worksheet.

[08:28] Daniel Reyes: Is the model execution deterministic across lanes? We don't want model behavior to change when we move from Hosted to Dedicated.

[08:36] Liam O'Connor: We surface the same model versions across lanes; there can be minor differences due to quantization or kernel selection on different hardware. We document model variant IDs and recommend smoke tests during cutover.

[08:52] Aria Patel: Okay, on the MSA redline: we'll highlight the data deletion clause and training carveouts; Tom will add indemnity language and Sasha will add the audit scope. Expect those comments in the doc early next week.

[09:05] Tom Wu: One administrative thing — we need a test account, or a staging environment to kick the tires before the pilot. Can Redwood provision a sandbox with realistic quotas?

[09:15] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provision a sandbox with the demo model and traffic patterns. We'll include a test token bundle for a two-week trial aligned to the pilot. Liam will set it up with the telemetry hooks.

[09:28] Maggie Ortiz: For billing, can we get an estimate of monthly cost for 5M tokens/day average with 3x spikes during campaign windows?

[09:38] Liam O'Connor: We'll model three scenarios: Hosted on-demand, Dedicated reserved commit for baseline, Dedicated + burst credits. The pricing worksheet will show per-token delta and amortized infra costs.

[09:52] Daniel Reyes: Security question — do you have support for customer-supplied HSM via AWS CloudHSM or Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys?

[10:00] Jon Park: For Private yes. For Dedicated we can integrate with AWS KMS and customer keys in a bring-your-own-KMS pattern but full HSM-level isolation is typically Private/on-prem. We'll list supported key providers.

[10:15] Aria Patel: Any restrictions on data egress when using Private? We want to ensure no telemetry leaves our VPC.

[10:24] Priya Nambiar: In Private, telemetry and logs stay in your environment; Redwood's control plane can be run in a customer-managed VPC or we can do a disconnected deployment. We'll document network flows.

[10:40] Maya Chen: Quick recap — action items and timings: I'll send MSA redline 11/27, SOC2 + ISO links 11/26, pricing sheet 11/29, bench numbers 11/30. BlueLattice will push back MSA comments by 11/30 and confirm lane by 12/02. Pilot kickoff targeted first week of Dec.

[11:05] Aria Patel: That works. We'll try to get legal comments prioritized. If possible include a short one-page summary of the MSA impact areas for finance.

[11:18] Maggie Ortiz: Also please call out any non-recurring onboarding fees so FP&A can model.

[11:28] Maya Chen: Will do. Anything else?

[11:34] Tom Wu: One last ask — include a short failover story: if you lose a region, what are the failover times and when does failover incur cross-region egress charges?

[11:44] Priya Nambiar: Good point. We'll include an RTO/RPO table and egress implications per failover scenario.

[11:55] Sasha Kline: Thanks — appreciate the clarity so far.

[12:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.

[12:07] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings - e.g., "KV cache" was transcribed a few times as "KV cash"; speaker label Lindsay vs Liam once mismatched in the auto transcript and edited here. References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.ai/bluelattice/onboarding-deck), pricing worksheet (placeholder link sent in chat).
